[word/document.xml] Construction and Field Operations Manual

[word/document.xml] The nominal 4 ft x 8 ft sideline screen provides the color guard with a concealed area for storing equipment and making costume or equipment changes. The frame is constructed from 3/4-in. EMT conduit, off-the-shelf brackets, and 3D-printed parts. Decorative vinyl covers the finished face. The completed screen folds flat for transport and storage and unfolds for field deployment.

[word/document.xml] Field Operations

[word/document.xml] Appendix A is the field-facing portion of the manual. It is designed to be printed and carried independently by student field operators, parent pit crew, and logistics handlers responsible for transport, field staging, deployment, ballasting, and safety abort protocols.

[word/document.xml] • Rapid Folding Sequence: To fold a deployed screen flat for transport, handlers disengage the two 3D-printed hinged arm clips (I) from the lower inner cross rail (Rail 3), swing the bottom support arms (E) upward against the rear frame, and collapse the entire rear support frame (D/C) flat against the main frame. The vinyl banner remains taut and undisturbed.

[word/document.xml] • Coplanar Internal Nesting (≤ 2.0" Folded Thickness): The duck blind is engineered so that all rear support arms (D), rear cross rail (C), and bottom support arms (E) collapse completely coplanar inside the perimeter framing. When folded flat, the screen is no more than 2.0 inches thick, with the 3D-printed hinged arm clips (I) representing the thickest feature of the folded assembly. Consequently, 8 folded screens require only 16.0 inches of cart bed width, leaving over 28 inches of deck space on the 44.5-inch transport cart for staged sandbags and guide dividers.

[word/document.xml] • Dedicated Rolling Cart Loading: Folded screens are loaded vertically onto the dedicated rolling transport cart between side guide rails. Front and rear retaining gates are closed and latched (using the 3D-printed Cart Gate Latches) to lock the stack securely in place for smooth rolling between the equipment trailer and stadium staging areas.
-[word/document.xml] 1.2 Field Routing, 3-Person Crew Architecture, and Pincer Deployment Protocol
+[word/document.xml] 1.2 Field Routing, Pre-Set Receiver Architecture, and Deployment Protocol

[word/document.xml] • CBA Rule 5.02 Mandatory Rear Entrance Rule: CRITICAL RULES COMPLIANCE — Even though Sideline Screens are placed along the front sideline flanking the front ensemble, CBA Rule 5.02 strictly mandates that ALL PROPS MUST ENTER THE PERFORMANCE FIELD FROM THE BACK SIDELINE OR REAR END ZONE GATES (above the goal posts). Entering directly across the front boundary is strictly reserved for front ensemble equipment personnel and soloists. Handlers must roll the transport cart through the rear entrance gate and transit along the field perimeter around to their front sideline coordinates. Crossing directly onto the field from the front is a direct boundary violation.

[word/document.xml] • Front Sideline Placement Coordinates: The full competition fleet consists of 16 screens total, deployed in two 8-screen lines flanking the front ensemble (pit): Side 1 (Left / Stage Right) with 8 screens spanning ~64 ft along the front sideline from approx. the 20 to 41-yard line; and Side 2 (Right / Stage Left) with 8 screens spanning ~64 ft from approx. the 59 to 80-yard line. Screens conceal auxiliary color guard equipment, prop flags, quick-change items, and auxiliary instruments.

-[word/document.xml] • Dedicated 3-Person Cart Crew Architecture: Field deployment is executed by a dedicated 3-person crew per transport cart (single cart = 3 handlers; dual carts flanking Side 1 and Side 2 = two 3-person crews, 6 handlers total). Each member performs a strictly coordinated function to minimize field occupancy: Person 1 serves as Cart Driver and Egress Lead; Person 2 serves as Offloader and Opposite-End Deployer; Person 3 serves as Trailing Deployer.

-[word/document.xml] • Coordinated "Pincer" Deployment Choreography: 1) Driver (Person 1) pushes the loaded cart from the rear entrance gate along the perimeter to the front sideline placement zone; 2) Offloader (Person 2) walks alongside, sliding folded screens from the cart and dropping them flat on the turf at rough coordinate marks (25, 30, 35, 40 yd); 3) Trailing Deployer (Person 3) follows behind, immediately executing final setup on Screen 1 (swings rear triangle open, snaps the two clips into Rail 3, places rear rail ballast); 4) As soon as the final screen is deposited, Driver (Person 1) rolls the empty cart completely off the performance field across the front boundary into sideline staging; 5) Offloader (Person 2) moves to that far end of the screen line and deploys inward, meeting Trailing Deployer (Person 3) in the middle in a converging pincer movement; 6) Both handlers verify ballast, then step across the front sideline boundary together.

-[word/document.xml] • Extrapolated Field Timeline for 8 Screens Per Cart vs. CBA Rule 5.06 (3:15 Clock): Under CBA Rule 5.06, the band has exactly 3 minutes 15 seconds (195 seconds) from entry permission until the introductory announcement ends. With two 3-person crews operating dedicated 8-screen carts concurrently, timings on athletic turf demonstrate high efficiency: Perimeter Ingress requires ~65 seconds for Side 1 (~220 ft) and ~85 seconds for Side 2 (~300 ft with far-side transit); Drop-and-Go Deposition of 8 screens across the 64-ft span requires ~48 seconds (cart drivers exit field over the front boundary at t = 1:55 on Side 1 and t = 2:15 on Side 2); Pincer Setup Convergence with each handler deploying 4 screens in parallel requires ~48–55 seconds; Final Crew Clearance requires ~10 seconds. Total field setup is fully completed in ~2:30 (150s) for Side 1 and ~2:50 (170s) for Side 2. This leaves a reliable 25 to 45-second safety buffer before the announcement finishes, eliminating Rule 4.03 adult field-presence penalties.

+[word/document.xml] • Dedicated Fleet & Pre-Set Receiver Architecture: Field operations are executed by a dedicated 2-cart fleet (Cart 1 = Side 1; Cart 2 = Side 2; 8 screens and 8 ballast bags per cart) supported by an integrated adult and student performer crew: 2 Adult Cart Pushers (1 adult pushing each cart); 2 Student Unloaders (1 student jogging alongside each cart to pull folded blinds from racks); 16 Pre-Show Screen Setters (students whose opening drill set Dot 1 is directly adjacent to each screen location on the front sideline); and 16 Post-Show Egress Performers (students whose closing drill set finishes adjacent to each screen). This role separation eliminates cross-field transit and minimizes adult field occupancy.

+[word/document.xml] • Continuous Deployment Choreography & Asymmetric Backfield Staging: 1) Asymmetric Staging: Before entry, logistics identifies the stadium exit gate; both carts stage on the backfield marker closest to the exit (Exit-Side Cart stages at the 20-yd line; Far-Side Cart stages at the 40-yd line), giving both pushers a direct 55-yd straight lane to the front sideline; 2) Directional Ingress: At permission to enter (T = 0:00), adult pushers roll carts straight forward across the field to the front sideline, turn 90°, and roll away from the exit (Exit side rolls 22 to 42 yd; Far side rolls 42 to 22 yd); 3) The Drop: As each cart rolls, the student unloader pulls one folded blind every 2.7 yards and drops it flat on the turf—the cart never stops; 4) Parallel Setup: Pre-set student setters waiting at their marks immediately catch their blind, unfold the triangular frame, and snap internal brace clips into place in parallel (~6s each); 5) Parked for Egress: Carts drop their final blind and step just outside the front boundary into parking, finishing deployment already stationed at the exact locations required for post-show ballast collection (Exit side parked at 42; Far side parked at 22).

+[word/document.xml] • Operational Field Timeline vs. CBA Rule 5.06 (3:15 Clock): Under CBA Rule 5.06, the band has exactly 3 minutes 15 seconds (195 seconds) from entry permission until the introductory announcement ends. Operating two dedicated 8-screen carts in parallel with pre-set student receivers completes total field setup in ~2 minutes 14 seconds (134 seconds): straight 55-yd backfield charge requires ~50 seconds; continuous drop line requires ~25 seconds; parallel student latching requires ~6 seconds; and adult pushers clear the boundary into park positions by ~1:35. This enables the director to signal the Timing & Penalties judge ~60 seconds early, cueing the introductory announcement and banking an extra minute into the post-show clearance budget while eliminating any risk of Rule 4.03 adult field-presence penalties.
[word/document.xml] 1.3 Handler Training & High-Wind Emergency Abort Protocol

[word/document.xml] • Crew Sizing: Each sideline screen is handled by no fewer than two student operators during field transit and placement. On steep inclines (Falcon Stadium concrete tunnel ramp) or breezy days, assign 3 to 4 handlers to the transport cart.

[word/document.xml] • High-Wind Field Abort (Tier 4 Thresholds): If sustained winds exceed 20 mph or peak gusts exceed 25 mph, field operations are STRICT NO-GO. If sudden severe gusts strike while on the field, handlers immediately disengage the two hinged arm clips (I), fold the rear support frame flat against the main frame, and lay the entire screen flat on the turf. Per CBA Rule 4.02(a), authorized adult volunteers with Rule 9.07 Field Pass wristbands may enter the field solely to hold or secure props in dangerous winds.
[word/document.xml] • Rule 8.07 & 8.08 (Wheels & 12-Foot Height Limit): Pneumatic-like tires required on carts; 12-foot rigid height limit strictly observed (screen is 4 ft height when deployed).
[word/document.xml] • Rule 9.07 (25 Field Pass Wristbands): Access restricted to designated wristbands (max 25 per band upon check-in; field-only access). Separate colors for Prelims vs Finals.
[word/document.xml] 1.6 Post-Use Egress, Inspection & Storage

-[word/document.xml] • Continuous Uphill Egress: Upon show conclusion, handlers immediately disengage hinged arm clips (I), collapse screens flat, load onto transport cart, latch retaining gates, and roll the cart off the field in continuous movement up to the trailer staging lot per Rule 8.05. Do not de-ballast or park carts in stadium exit chutes.

+[word/document.xml] • Five-Step Field Egress Protocol & Zero Doubling Back: 1) Final Chord (T = 0:00): The 16 designated egress performers simultaneously unclip internal braces and collapse the 3-panel frames flat (~6s); 2) Ballast Removal & Hand-Carry Sprint: Performers remove the 15-lb ballast sandbag from the frame base and leave it in place resting on the turf—being careful not to throw or drop them (protecting bag seams and turf). Each performer picks up their 26-lb folded frame and jogs directly down the sideline corridor into the stadium exit chute or tunnel (35–50s); 3) Zero-Doubling-Back Ballast Sweep: Adult pushers step onto the sideline from their park spots and sweep ballast bags strictly in the direction of the exit: Exit-Side Cart sweeps outward (42 to 22 yd) toward the gate; Far-Side Cart sweeps inward (22 to 42 yd) toward midfield and the exit chute. Carts sprint into the exit with zero wasted backward travel; 4) Clock Stop: At standard venues, the 15:00 clock stops when the last prop, cart, and performer physically clears the perimeter gate (with a 45-second buffer absorbing gate bottlenecks); at Falcon Stadium, the clock stops upon entering the tunnel mouth; 5) Off-Clock Cart Reload: Inside the Falcon Stadium tunnel mouth or trailer staging lot, folded screens are reloaded into cart racks and lashed down completely off the competition clock while the next band takes the field.

[word/document.xml] • Two-Shot Competition Protocol: Between Prelims and Finals, screens remain stacked on the transport cart in the trailer lot. If afternoon gusts increase, keep screens folded flat on the cart bed to eliminate sail area while maintaining readiness for Finals.
[word/document.xml] PART OF THE SIDELINE SCREEN / DUCK BLIND CONSTRUCTION AND FIELD OPERATIONS MANUAL
[word/document.xml] APPENDIX B

[word/document.xml] • High-Wind Emergency Lay-Flat: If severe gusts strike (>25 mph), handlers disengage hinged arm clips (I), fold rear support frame flat, and lay screens flat on turf. Adult volunteers with Rule 9.07 wristbands may assist per Rule 4.02(a).
[word/document.xml] 3. Rapid Field Deployment & Teardown Checklist

[word/document.xml] • Venue Staging & Ingress: Screens are transported fully assembled on cart. Roll cart to rear gate. When T&P judge signals entry permission, roll cart along perimeter to front sideline placement zone.

-[word/document.xml] • 3-Person Pincer Deployment & Egress: 1) Driver pushes cart from rear gate; 2) Offloader drops screens at coordinates; 3) Trailing deployer & offloader converge in pincer setup (swing triangle, snap clips into Rail 3, set rail C ballast); 4) Driver rolls empty cart off field; 5) Handlers clear field (~2:20 setup, +50s buffer before 3:15 clock ends). At show conclusion, unclip E arms, fold into cart, and maintain continuous egress up hill to lot per Rule 8.05.

+[word/document.xml] • Pre-Set Receiver Deployment & Egress: 1) Carts stage on back 20/40 marks; 2) Pushers roll 55 yd straight across field, turn away from exit, and roll dropping blinds; 3) Pre-set students at marks latch frames in parallel (~2:14 setup, banks +60s); 4) Post-show, performers collapse frames, leave ballast on turf (do not throw/drop), and hand-carry frames to exit; 5) Pushers sweep ballast straight toward exit with zero doubling back; 6) Reload carts off-clock in tunnel or lot per Rule 8.05.

[word/document.xml] • Continuous Uphill Egress & Double-Bagging (Rule 8.05): Following the performance, all props and equipment must remain in continuous movement until entirely removed from the stadium. NEVER stop or de-ballast carts at the stadium exit chute or tunnel—maintain momentum up the incline to the trailer lot. All sandbags must be double-bagged with intact plastic inner liners.
[word/document.xml] 3. Essential Volunteer Handling & Safety Checkpoints
[word/document.xml] • Fully Assembled Transport: Screens are transported fully assembled on cart; zero tools, bolts, or frame assembly required on site.

-[word/document.xml] • 3-Person Pincer Deployment: 1 person drives cart; 1 person offloads and drops screens roughly; trailing person deploys and ballasts. Driver rolls empty cart off field; offloader deploys from far end inward to meet trailing deployer in the middle (~2:20 setup; 50s safety buffer before 3:15 clock ends).

-[word/document.xml] • Fleet & Crew Sizing: 16 screens total across 2 transport carts (8 screens per cart); 3 handlers per cart crew (6 total); assign 3 to 4 handlers on carts navigating steep inclines (Falcon Stadium ramp).
